Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Zinvolt. It reads the **Zinvolt
batteries** of your account through the Zinvolt cloud service, with the
e-mail and password you use in the Zinvolt app.

**Never tested with a real device**: it was built from the
[python-zinvolt](https://github.com/joostlek/python-zinvolt) library (the one
of Home Assistant) and its test answers. Please report what you see on a real
battery.

## What you get

One device per battery of the account (10 at most), with:

- state of charge (%);
- the socket power (W, signed): what the device exchanges with the home at
  its socket, solar included. It is **not** the power of the battery
  itself: with 500 W of solar, 300 W into the battery and 200 W to the home,
  it reads +200 W while the battery charges. Positive towards the home,
  negative from it; this sign follows Home Assistant (its Zinvolt sensor
  shows the opposite of the `pso` value of the API) and is **still to be
  confirmed** on a real battery. This version has no battery charge or
  discharge power: the API does not give it with a known sign;
- solar power (W), and the power given to the home through the socket (W,
  the positive part of the socket power, same sign to confirm);
- online, on grid and dormant states (1 = yes, 0 = no);
- the smart mode (0 = default, 1 = self use, 2 = dynamic, 3 = charged,
  4 = performance, 5 = feed, 6 = custom);
- the settings: maximum output, charge upper and discharge lower limits,
  maximum charge power, standby time, and the system power limit.

**Read-only**: the integration never changes the mode, the output, the
limits nor anything else of the battery.

**No energy counter**: the Zinvolt API gives powers only, no kWh. The
integration adds nothing to the energy monitoring of Gladys and never makes
up an energy from a power.

An offline battery (or one whose online state is unknown or contradictory)
only gets its online state and its settings: its last live values are never
sent again as new ones.

## Configuration

1. In Gladys, open the integration, **Configuration** tab.
2. Enter the **e-mail** and the **password** of your Zinvolt account. The
   password is kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again; it is
   sent only to the Zinvolt service, in its login request, never logged.
3. Keep the **reading interval** at 60 s, or more. One read is one request
   for the list, one per battery, and a login when the session needs one.
4. Save, then create the devices from the **Discover** tab.

## Behaviour

- Never a read faster than the interval: not the test button, not Discovery,
  not a reconnection, not a save of an unchanged form, not a restart (the
  time of the last request is kept in `/data`).
- **Refused e-mail or password**: the reads stop and stay stopped, even after
  a restart; there is no new automatic try (an account could get locked).
  Enter another password, or click **Test the connection** to try once:
  saving the same password again tries nothing.
- **Account accepted but access to the API refused** (the service refuses
  the session it has just opened, for instance an account without access to
  the API): the same final stop, kept in `/data`, never a login in a loop.
  Check the account in the Zinvolt app, then click **Test the connection**,
  or enter other credentials.
- An expired session gets one new login per read at most.
- **Too many requests or an error of the service**: the reads pause from 1
  minute to 6 hours (kept in `/data`). A battery that fails alone is only left
  out of that read.
- `/data` never keeps the e-mail, the password nor the session: only a salted
  fingerprint of the account, and of refused credentials while they are
  refused.
- Each answer must name the serial number of the battery it was asked for;
  an answer naming another one is left out. A battery listed without a
  readable identifier is left out too, and the status says so.

## Troubleshooting

- The status of the integration says what happened and when the next read is.
- The socket power looks inverted (negative while the home gets power from
  the device, with no solar)? Its sign has not been checked on a real
  battery yet: please report it. With solar, a positive socket power while
  the battery charges is normal (see above).

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt Zinvolt in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Zinvolt | `section` | Nein | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Zinvolt. It reads the batteries of your Zinvolt account through the Zinvolt cloud service, with the e-mail and password of the Zinvolt app, every 60 seconds: state of charge, power at the socket (signed, sign to confirm) and to the home, solar power, online and grid state, smart mode and settings. Read-only: it never changes the mode, the output or the charge limits. No energy counter: the API gives powers only. Never tested with a real device. |
| E-mail of the Zinvolt account | `string` | Ja | The e-mail you sign in with in the Zinvolt app. |
| Password of the Zinvolt account | `secret` | Ja | Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again; sent only to the Zinvolt service, in its login request, never logged. If Zinvolt refuses it, the reads stop with no automatic try: enter another password (saving the same one again tries nothing), or click the test button to try once. |
| Reading interval (s) | `number` | Nein | How often the account is read (one request plus one per battery): 60 s by default, more if you wish. Nothing reads it faster, not even the test button. |

## So installierst du Zinvolt in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: Zinvolt erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-zinvolt:0.1.1`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-zinvolt](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-zinvolt).

Zinvolt benötigt Gladys `>=5.2.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

Zinvolt ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
